security_spec.violation_condition: XiangShan RTL implements Smidctrl/Ssidctrl with hardwired eidelivery=0x20000000 (ACLIC-only mode) and an eithreshold CSR that applies only to interrupt priority levels, but software following the updated spec attempts to use the new mithreshold CSR (which applies to both major and minor interrupt identities) for priority ceiling synchronization. The hardware either (a) ignores writes to mithreshold because the decoder routes threshold through the old eithreshold register, or (b) applies old threshold semantics that do not filter on minor interrupt identities, allowing low-priority minor interrupts to preempt critical sections protected by Priority Ceiling Protocol.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: search for CSR decode logic where (eithreshold CSR address is decoded but mithreshold is not) OR (eidelivery is hardwired to constant 0x20000000 via WireInit/RegInit) OR (interrupt threshold comparator only checks priority bits but not major/minor identity fields)
security_spec.summary: Removal of eithreshold/eidelivery from Smidctrl scope and introduction of mithreshold with major+minor identity thresholding creates a semantic mismatch: RTL hardwiring old eidelivery ACLIC-only mode or implementing old priority-only eithreshold will silently break interrupt priority ceiling enforcement, allowing untrusted interrupts to escape threshold gating

findings.finding: mithreshold CSR (address 0x347 per ACLIC spec Smidctrl section) is NOT defined in the CSR address decode table. The CSR address 0x347 has no entry in CSRs.scala. Software writes to mithreshold will take the default read-as-zero/write-ignored path, meaning the interrupt-enable threshold is permanently zero — all pending-enabled interrupts are always deliverable regardless of priority ceiling. This silently defeats Priority Ceiling Protocol synchronization.

spec_citations.excerpt:
Number  Name         Description
 (NEW) 0x347   mithreshold  Interrupt enable threshold

A new WLRL M-mode CSR, mithreshold, determines the priority cutoff used to mask lower-priority interrupts... In contrast to existing threshold mechanisms in AIA, this CSR applies to major and minor interrupt identities.

findings.finding: The complete AIA CSR module list (aiaCSRMods) contains only miselect, mireg, mtopei, mtopi, siselect, sireg, stopei, stopi, vsiselect, vsireg, vstopi, vstopei. No mithreshold, sithreshold, mpistatus, spistatus, or mipreemptcfg CSR modules exist. Any Smidctrl/Ssidctrl CSR access falls through to the default illegal-instruction or read-as-zero path. The mireg indirect access range declared illegal at 0x40-0x6F blocks the IMSIC-style eithreshold/eidelivery address space — confirming the RTL supports neither IMSIC threshold CSRs nor ACLIC threshold CSRs.
findings.snippet:
val aiaCSRMods = Seq(
  miselect, mireg, mtopei, mtopi,
  siselect, sireg, stopei, stopi,
  vsiselect, vsireg, vstopi, vstopei,
)

spec_citations.excerpt: The AIA eidelivery and eithreshold CSRs defined for the IMSIC are not included in the scope of Smidctrl/Ssidctrl... Therefore, no dynamic selection of ACLIC operation via eidelivery is provided.

findings.finding: Interrupt delivery gating (mIRVecTmp, hsIRVecTmp, vsIRVecTmp) checks ONLY privilege mode (isModeM/isModeHS/isModeVS) and global interrupt-enable bits (mstatusMIE/sstatusSIE/vsstatusSIE). There is NO interrupt threshold comparison. In a spec-compliant Smidctrl/Ssidctrl implementation with mithreshold, an interrupt should be delivered only when IPRIO < xithreshold & NIPPRIO_MASK. The absence of threshold comparison means all pending-enabled interrupts are always deliverable — low-priority interrupts will preempt critical sections protected by Priority Ceiling Protocol with no hardware enforcement.

spec_citations.excerpt: When xithreshold is a nonzero value, an interrupt source is considered disabled irrespective of its interrupt-enable bit, when: IPRIO >= xithreshold & NIPPRIO_MASK

findings.finding: The pending-interrupt check (mtopiIsNotZero) is a pure bitwise AND of mip, mie, and ~mideleg with no threshold filtering. Per the ACLIC spec, when mithreshold is nonzero, interrupts with IPRIO >= mithreshold & NIPPRIO_MASK should be treated as disabled even if their pending and enable bits are set. This check unconditionally reports 'interrupt pending' whenever any enabled interrupt source is pending, regardless of the threshold value.

spec_citations.excerpt: When xithreshold is a nonzero value, an interrupt source is considered disabled irrespective of its interrupt-enable bit, when the following condition holds: IPRIO >= xithreshold & NIPPRIO_MASK

findings.finding: The IpriosSort priority bundle uses a flat 8-bit prioNum without major/minor interrupt identity decomposition. The ACLIC spec defines mithreshold to apply to BOTH major and minor interrupt identities for Priority Ceiling Protocol enforcement (NIPPRIO_MASK filters bits to determine which priority bits participate in preemption decisions). Without major/minor identity fields, threshold comparison cannot distinguish between interrupts in different identity groups that happen to have numerically similar priority values — low-priority minor interrupts within the same major group could bypass threshold filtering.
findings.snippet:
class IpriosSort extends Bundle {
  val idx = UInt(6.W)
  val enable = Bool()
  val isZero = Bool()
  val greaterThan255 = Bool()
  val prioNum = UInt(8.W)
}

spec_citations.excerpt: A mask for filtering out the bits of a priority number that will participate in the selection for nested interrupt preemption: NIPPRIO_MASK = ~(2^(mipreemptcfg.preemptmsk) - 1)
In contrast to existing threshold mechanisms in AIA, this CSR applies to major and minor interrupt identities.

findings.finding: The minSelect priority comparator (line 179) compares single flat 8-bit prioNum values: `Mux(left.prioNum <= right.prioNum, left, right)`. With mithreshold/NIPPRIO_MASK semantics, the comparator should apply the preempt mask to filter priority bits before comparing, so that only the bits selected by mipreemptcfg.preemptmsk participate in preemption decisions. Without masked comparison, all 8 priority bits influence preemption decisions regardless of the configured NIPPRIO_MASK.

The InterruptFilterIO input bundle has no threshold field (no mithreshold value input). The output bundle has no xithreshold update output. Per ACLIC spec, on interrupt entry: xithreshold must be set to IPRIO (automatically raising the threshold), and xpistatus.pithreshold must be set to the previous threshold value. On xRET: xithreshold must be restored from xpistatus.pithreshold. Without these signals in the IO bundle, the hardware cannot implement the spec-mandated automatic threshold management during trap entry/return.

spec_citations.excerpt: When a trap is taken into level x, the current value of xithreshold is written to xpistatus.pithreshold. Additionally, if the trap was taken on an interrupt, xithreshold is set to IPRIO.
xret sets xithreshold to xpistatus.pithreshold. This automatically restores the interrupt-enable threshold to the level of the previous context.

findings.finding: The InterruptFilter is wired with all standard interrupt signals (mip, mie, mideleg, miprios, hsiprios, mtopei, stopei, vstopei, hvictl, hstatus, hviprio1, hviprio2) but NO threshold CSR is connected because no such CSR exists. The CSR-to-InterruptFilter wiring lacks the essential feedback path where (a) the InterruptFilter reads the current mithreshold value to gate interrupt delivery, and (b) the InterruptFilter updates mithreshold/mpistatus on trap entry/return.
findings.snippet:
intrMod.io.in.mtopei := mtopei.regOut
intrMod.io.in.stopei := stopei.regOut
intrMod.io.in.vstopei := vstopei.regOut
intrMod.io.in.miprios := Cat(miregiprios.map(_.rdata).reverse)
intrMod.io.in.hsiprios := Cat(siregiprios.map(_.rdata).reverse)
// NO threshold CSR wiring — no mithreshold, mpistatus, or mipreemptcfg connection
